body: I've re-added this line because all the workflows throw the same error: `callable_mp not found`. My own fork compiles just fine so I assume something is changed in master.

This feels a bit complicated. Assuming the ID can be discarded each time, it might be better to iterate through all tracks without retaining previous IDs, checking only if the same cache type exists.

One way to do this, I though it might be a bit of a hack, but you can convert every concatenated path to StringName first, then use only the memory address of the StringName as the int ID. In other words, it guarantees no duplication by allocating all StringName objects in memory only during iteration, then releases the StringName area after using them as IDs.

Well, I understand it should work. I'll ask others for their opinions to see if there's a better approach, and if this is acceptable, we can proceed with the merge. Do you have any idea @Ryan-000 @Ivorforce ?

If the issue is hash collisions, I would use `TrackCacheId` (the  `Pair<NodePath, TrackType>`) in `AnimationMixer::track_cache` so it would look like this `AHashMap<TrackCacheId, TrackCache *>`.

Since https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116394 changes the implementation of `AnimationMixer::_blend_calc_total_weight`  and removes `thread_local HashSet<Animation::TypeHash, HashHasher> processed_hashes;` (assuming that makes it in), then the per frame performance shouldn't really change. 

Code related to `AnimatedValuesBackup` like `AnimationMixer::_build_backup_track_cache()` might be a bit slower, but that should be ok since its editor code.

And `AnimationMixer::_update_caches()` also might get a bit slower, but since it not called every frame, it also should be fine.

Also, `Animation::track_cache_id_map` is not thread safe and will cause issues in projects using [group-based threaded scene processing](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6424), or `ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request` and C# projects that reference animation objects (since the resource may be freed on the .NET Finalizer thread).

I tested this along with `Pair<NodePath, TrackType>` with the current master (using thash). Again, using the same mrp:


|  | Master (uint32_t thash) | Master (uint64_t thash) | Pair | StringName |
|--------|------------|--------|--------|--------|

I just changed the `typedef` for `Pair`. So I think using the `Pair` is out of question (and maybe it was the culprit for the previous ID assignment overhead).

For StringName, I kept the `StringName path_with_type` in the track to make it stay in the memory and used its pointer as key (casted to `uint64_t`). In the PR description, I provided my initial benchmarks which included StringName as key (not the pointer), therefore I did not make another benchmark for it, assuming it would be worse anyways.

I didn't want to give up any performance, but at this point I don't think it can be avoided. The thread safety ruins everything. Now I'm leaning towards `StringName` as well.

As `uint64_t` version of master performs better, I think with some tweaks, the `StringName` pointer can give a similar performance as well. More importantly, it should eliminate thread safety concerns. Is this OK?

Looks good to me so far.

My only concern at this point is `AnimatedValuesBackup`. Right now it relies on `TypeHash`, but with this change `TypeHash` is effectively based on `StringName::data_unique_pointer()`, so it is only stable for as long as the backing `StringName` remains alive.

I think this could break in a case like this:
- `AnimationMixer::make_backup()` stores values keyed by `TypeHash`.
- Later, the relevant `Animation` resources are unloaded, along with their `Track`s and possibly the backing `StringName`s.
- If those animations are loaded again, `path_with_cache_type` may end up with a different `data_unique_pointer()`.
- At that point, `AnimationMixer::restore()` could be working with stale keys from `AnimatedValuesBackup` that no longer match the current mixer state.

Because of that, I think `AnimatedValuesBackup` should eventually use a stable identifier across unload/reload, such as `StringName` itself or `Pair<NodePath, TrackType>`, instead of `TypeHash`.

That said, I think this can be handled later once we have @TokageItLab's opinion on the current approach and when the PR is updated.
